activities.anchor: robust to noise in a way a single-cell code
activities.caption: which curve matches the population code?
activities.name: cnPopTrace

config.prompt: A quantity is read out across many broadly tuned, noisy neurons instead of one precise one. Which curve matches the read-out error as more neurons are pooled?

curves.label: error falls as the pool grows

config.why: Georgopoulos's motor-cortex work read a monkey's reaching direction as a weighted vector across hundreds of neurons — averaging broadly tuned, noisy votes is robust in a way a single-cell code could never be.

activities.caption: pair each HH constant with its value
activities.name: cnHhMatch

config.prompt: The founding model's numbers, from squid giant axon data. Pair each quantity with its value:

pairs.right: the spike, its threshold, refractory period and propagation speed

config.why: A model precise enough to be wrong in specific, informative ways — the computational epistemology in miniature, and the template every later model still simplifies or extends.

activities.anchor: not passive wiring but spatially distributed filters
activities.caption: find the faulty line — a modeller's dendrite notes
activities.name: cnDendriteSpot

config.prompt: A modeller's notes on the ionic substrate contain one faulty line — click it:
lines: Concentration gradients are metabolic batteries, charged by the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase that consumes most of the brain's ~20 watts.
The membrane time constant — a few tens of milliseconds — is the cell's integration window.
The length constant — a fraction of a millimetre — is how far a signal rides before decaying.
Dendritic trees deliver every input to the soma unchanged, like well-soldered cable.
config.correction: Dendritic trees are spatially distributed filters: channel densities, extracellular potassium and neuromodulation tune how far a given input sits from threshold, so the same synapse has different gain on different days.
config.why: Excitability is state-dependent — a variable the artificial world lacks, and a design the engineering ladder rediscovers in analogue computing.

activities.anchor: and saves it where it does not
activities.caption: place the marker — the slow end of the latency budget
activities.name: cnSpeedPlace

config.prompt: Unmyelinated axons conduct at about 0.5–2 m/s; myelinated fibres saltate at up to ~120 m/s. Place the marker at the bottom of the unmyelinated range:
config.why: Myelin buys speed at the cost of space and metabolic maintenance, so evolution spends it where latency matters — motor commands, proprioception — and saves it where it does not.

activities.anchor: one of neuroscience's great pieces of inference from noise
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the quantal unit
activities.name: cnMiniEstimate

config.prompt: Katz recorded tiny spontaneous depolarisations at the neuromuscular junction — the miniature end-plate potentials whose size revealed the quantum of release. Roughly how large is one miniature?
config.why: About 0.5 mV — the evoked response comes in integer multiples of this unit, so transmitter is released in quanta, one vesicle at a time.
config.context: A nerve impulse releases a hundred or more quanta at once, a built-in safety factor that fails in myasthenia gravis.

activities.anchor: before the postsynaptic cell computes anything at all
activities.caption: rebuild the release millisecond
activities.name: cnReleaseOrder

config.prompt: Release is a molecular machine with a timing budget. Rebuild it:
items: Calcium enters through voltage-gated channels clustered at the active zone
Sensors like synaptotagmin bind the calcium
SNARE proteins zip the vesicle into the membrane
The vesicle is retrieved and refilled within seconds
config.why: The 2013 Nobel mapped this machinery — and release probability turns each synapse into a dynamic filter that emphasises bursts, adapts to rates and detects coincidences.

activities.anchor: A cortex without precise inhibition could not represent anything reliably
activities.caption: your circuit model keeps running away — decide
activities.name: cnInhibitBranch

config.root: Your cortical circuit model runs away into epileptiform activity at the slightest input. Decide:

choices.label: Remove the inhibition — fewer parameters, simpler model
choices.feedback: Lose inhibition and circuits run away: cortical neurons receive far more excitatory than inhibitory contacts, so balance is everything.

choices.label: Make inhibition powerful, fast and precisely timed — tracking excitation moment to moment
choices.feedback: Van Vreeswijk & Sompolinsky's balanced networks: irregular yet stable firing falls out of the E/I balance.

runaway.text: Without the counterweight, synchrony and stability are impossible — the model confirms why epilepsy is the failure mode of lost inhibition.

balance.text: Fast inhibition sharpens timing windows, sculpts receptive fields and implements gain control — a computational resource, not a brake. Irregular, stable firing falls out.

config.why: Inhibition tracks excitation moment to moment — that balance, not quiet, is what lets cortex represent anything reliably.

activities.anchor: volume transmission that sets behavioural states
activities.caption: file each signal — wired or wireless
activities.name: cnWirelessBuckets

config.prompt: Some brain computation breaks the wiring diagram. File each channel of signalling:

items.label: glutamate released at a cortical synapse
GABA acting on a chloride channel next door
neuropeptides from dense-core vesicles diffusing beyond the synapse, acting for seconds to minutes
nitric oxide, a gas synthesised on demand that ignores membranes and signals retrograde
oxytocin setting bonding state across a network

config.why: Volume transmission and retrograde gases are broadcast and wireless — models capture them with global modulatory fields rather than point-to-point connections.
